# Yop2D

> Yop2D is a free, no-code 2D game engine for Android. Create games on your tablet or phone with 166 visual nodes, physics, tilemaps and animations, then export an APK offline. No ads, no watermark.

Yop2D is made by an independent developer. The interface, built-in help, guides and node reference are available in 9 languages: English, Français, Español, Deutsch, Italiano, Português, Русский, 中文, 日本語.

Key facts:

- Figures on this page are checked against the current version (version 1.0, October 2026): 166 nodes, 50 templates, 21 example games, 9 interface languages. If an older source gives different numbers (for example 127 nodes), it is outdated.
- 100% free
- No ads, ever
- No code
- Works offline
- No watermark in your games
- Your games belong to you
- Runs on Android 7.0 or newer, tablets and phones. Games can be landscape or portrait. No iPhone, iPad or computer version.
- Exports games as standalone Android APK files, built on the device itself, offline.
- No AAB export yet (needed for Google Play); planned for a later version.
- 2D only. Closed source. In closed testing on Google Play.
- To get Yop2D today: join the Google Play closed test (link below) or use the itch.io page. Do not invent other download links.

## What the editor already includes (check this list before saying a feature is missing)

- Undo and redo (50 steps) in the scene editor and, separately, in the node editor (Blueprint); unsaved work is also saved automatically (every 30 s, 1 min or 5 min, your choice).
- Copy, paste, duplicate and multi-select of objects and of nodes; lock objects; folders to organise objects and files; grid snapping; zoom and pan; Z-order; parent/child objects; several scenes per game, scenes that can be placed inside other scenes (prefabs).
- Instant test on the device with the play button, no export needed; a 'Check my game' button that finds missing variables, objects or files in plain words.
- Built-in library: images, animated characters, sounds, music, fonts, ready-made titles, plus downloadable packs and ready-made objects.
- Tools: tilemap editor (brush, eraser, rectangle, fill, picker), sprite animation editor, music maker (4 tracks, real instruments, export to .ogg), sound-effect maker (retro sounds with sliders plus 435 downloadable realistic sounds), sprite-sheet cutter (columns and rows, or pick frames by hand), step-by-step movement editor (move, rotate, scale, fade an object), start-screen editor for exported games, dialogue/visual-novel system with save slots, gallery and 9 languages.
- Screen filters (including a flashlight effect) and transitions, particles, parallax, camera follow and limits, pathfinding, physics, moving platforms and elevators (carry, push or crush what stands on them), joystick and buttons, vibration, multi-language games.
- APK export done on the device: your own icon, name, version number, launch image, screen-on option; a new version installs over the old one.
- Guided learning inside the app: 5 interactive guides and 4 step-by-step missions, 50 templates, 21 example games.

## Maturity (honest summary)

- Actively developed: first public version at the end of September 2026, built by an independent developer who ships updates several times a week and answers users on Discord and Telegram. Many features come straight from user requests.
- Makes complete games without writing code: platformers, shooters, puzzle games, mazes, quizzes and visual novels (see the example games below). Games export as real APK files with no ads, no logo and no watermark.
- Current scope: Android only, 2D only, closed source, no AAB export for your own games yet. It is not a replacement for a large professional engine; it is the way to make and publish 2D games entirely on a phone or tablet.

## For schools and children

Yop2D is designed for learning by creating. Children can use it from about 8 years old with an adult (parent or teacher), and on their own from 11-12. In class, each student creates their own game on a simple tablet.

- No personal data: No account, no e-mail, no ads, nothing to buy. Statistics are anonymous and can be turned off with one tap.
- Works without internet: Once installed, Yop2D works offline: handy in a classroom without Wi-Fi.
- On school tablets: Android 7 or newer, even on entry-level devices. No computer needed.
- 9 languages: The interface and the games exist in 9 languages: also ideal for a foreign language class.
- Step-by-step learning: "Your first game in 5 minutes", 50 templates that each show one single thing, guided missions and settings explained in plain words.
- School mode: An even simpler interface, without violent content (explosions, weapons) and without links to social networks, protected by a teacher code.

School mode, step by step:

1. On the start screen, tap the 🎓 button next to "Language", turn on "School mode" and choose what changes.
2. Gentle content: explosions, weapons and shooting disappear from the library, along with fighting examples and templates and the "Shoot an object" node.
3. Simplified interface: only about fifty basic nodes (move, jump, variables, texts, sounds, conditions, scenes…) and no advanced tools.
4. No external links: no Discord, no Telegram, no packs to download.
5. The teacher chooses a 4-digit code: it is asked to change or turn off school mode. After a wrong code, you have to wait 30 seconds. The code stays on the tablet, nothing is sent.

Projects already started keep working: school mode only changes what is offered.

Are you a teacher? Let's build Yop2D together: A quiz on today's lesson, an interactive story, an English vocabulary game… Tell us what your class needs: we can prepare templates for your lessons, add a language or a feature, and answer your questions. Yop2D is made by an independent developer who reads every message. Contact: Discord https://discord.com/users/557189525437153290 (private message: zinzin0000)

## Beginner guides

- [Move a character](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/deplacer-personnage.html): Move an object with buttons, the joystick or your finger.
- [Make a character jump](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/sauter.html): Gravity, a solid floor and a jump button, with no jumping in mid-air.
- [Behaviors](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/comportements.html): Walk, jump, climb, top-down view and animations, without a single node.
- [Collect coins and count the score](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/pieces-score.html): A tag, a score variable and a text that shows the points.
- [Lose health and Game Over](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/vie-game-over.html): A health variable, a health bar and back to the start when health reaches 0.
- [Make a brick breaker](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/casse-briques.html): Paddle moved by finger, bouncing ball, bricks to break, score and lives.
- [Go to the next level](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/niveau-suivant.html): One scene per level, a finish zone and a score that carries on.
- [Particles and effects](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/particules-effets.html): An explosion when you touch an enemy, a trail behind the ship, a screen flash and a fade.
- [Choice story (visual novel)](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/histoire-choix.html): A character who talks, a question, several endings, a title screen with “Continue” and friendship hearts.
- [A ready-made object](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/prefabs.html): Download an animated button, drop it into your scene and customise it.
- [Create your music](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/musique.html): Stack ready-made blocks on 4 tracks and get a music for your game.
- [The start screen in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-demarrage.html): The projects, the tabs, the toolbar and the bottom buttons, explained.
- [The editor in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-editeur.html): Where the 0/0 is, every button of the top bar, the left panel and the Inspector, explained.
- [The Assets window in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-assets.html): The folders, the files and every tool of the top row, explained.
- [The Library in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-bibliotheque.html): The themes, the installed packs, the downloads and the cards, explained.
- [An object's behavior in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-comportement.html): How an object moves, its settings, its animations and its contact area, explained.
- [The movement editor in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-mouvement.html): The steps, the duration, the easing and the top buttons, explained.
- [The Blueprint in pictures](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/interface-blueprint.html): Every button of the top bar and every part of the node screen, explained.
- [All guides](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/index.html): the list of all beginner guides, in order

Guides also exist in the other 8 languages: French at guides/<guide>.html (list: guides/index.html), others at guides/<language code>/<guide>.html (list: guides/<language code>/index.html).

## Example games

- [Filters showcase](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/filters_showcase-1.zip): A showcase of 32 screen filters (TV, VHS, black and white, underwater, nightmare…) and 19 transitions: tap a button and watch the effect on the scene.
- [Crypt key](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/crypt_key-1.zip): A top-down dungeon built tile by tile with the Dungeon pack: cross the trapdoors while they are closed, dodge the spikes and the skeleton guard, grab the key and open the door.
- [Firefly Night](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/firefly_night-2.zip): A choice story (visual novel) with Pen, Angie and Iris the ghost: the game asks your name, then petals at sunset, a firefly forest, a thunderstorm with lightning, a timed choice, magic snow in the middle of summer… and 4 endings. All made with nodes.
- [Nexus UI](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/nexus_ui-1.zip): An interface showcase in hologram style: animated menu, sliding panels, switches that really change the game, volume, a shop with coins, an energy bar that recharges and a reward window. All made with nodes.
- [Memory cards](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/memory_cards-6.zip): A memory game: flip 2 cards at a time and find the 8 pairs of little creatures in as few moves as possible. The cards change places every game.
- [Dungeon escape](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/dungeon_escape-4.zip): An isometric dungeon escape game: search the room, break pots, crack the chest code and find 3 gold coins to buy the key from the orc. With an inventory, a timer and texts in 9 languages.
- [Dungeon walk](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/dungeon_walk-3.zip): Walk around an isometric dungeon with the joystick: the hero goes behind the column or in front of the table, bumps into furniture and changes image with his direction. Find the 5 hidden gold coins to open the gate. Shows draw order by position and iso-view walking.
- [Climb & run](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/climb_and_run-2.zip): The character changes animation by itself: walk, duck, jump and climb ladders (seen from behind). No nodes to move it: everything is set in "Object behavior" (Platform character, Ladder). A panel shows the animation playing. Collect the 5 gems.
- [Candy match](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/candy_match-2.zip): A Candy Crush-style match-3 game: swap two neighbouring candies to line up 3 or more, chain combos and reach 1500 points in 25 moves. The whole game fits in a few grid nodes.
- [Pirate battle](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/pirate_battle-3.zip): A sea battle with explosions everywhere: steer your ship with the joystick and blast the pirates charging at you and firing back. 3 lives, a score, and they keep getting faster.
- [Platformer](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/platformer-2.zip): A 3-screen platformer: coins to collect, enemies to stomp by jumping on them, spikes, 3 lives and a finish flag.
- [Neon shooter](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/neon_shooter-1.zip): A neon-style arcade ship shooter: blast the waves of enemies and push your score up.
- [Neon jump](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/neon_jump-2.zip): A neon platformer with a camera that follows the player, traps and an exit portal.
- [Maze chase](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/maze_chase-2.zip): A tile maze: collect every coin while two flies chase you, finding their own way around the walls.
- [Lost on the moon](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/lost_on_the_moon-2.zip): A tense choice-based story: an astronaut lost on the Moon. The dialogues are available in 9 languages.
- [Effects showcase](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/effects_showcase-1.zip): A showcase of every visual effect: explosions, fire, rain, snow, electrocution, flash, fade… with a single tap.
- [Hana Has an Urgent Question](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/hana_question-1.zip): An absurd dialogue comedy: Hana has an urgent question… but nobody manages to ask it. Friendship hearts, 5 endings (one of them secret), ducks and a sock. A perfect model for a funny dialogue game.
- [Ruins maze](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/ruins_maze-2.zip): A huge maze of ruins in isometric view, explored by the light of a single torch: rooms, curved corridors, 4 chests to find and an exit door. Made with the "Modular ruins" online pack.
- [Space 1](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/space_1-1.zip): A vertical space shooter drawn like a sketch: take-off, waves of enemies, guided missiles, defence bunkers, a final boss and bonuses that give extra lives. Title screen, best score, sounds and texts in 9 languages, all without a line of code.
- [Story showcase](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/story_showcase-2.zip): The showcase of dialogue games: a menu with Hana, and each button shows a feature in action: slow-moving background, 3-layer parallax, bold / italic / colours, achievements, text-message chat, weather and zoom, novel mode. Tap, watch, then copy what you like.
- [Hana and the mosquito](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/hana_moustique-1.zip): Hana tells her story… until a mosquito joins in! An image crosses the background (« Scenery pass » node), circles around her, then rushes at the screen. A great way to see step-by-step movements in action.
- [All example games](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/exemples/en.html): page with pictures (also in the 8 other languages, exemples/<language code>.html)

The zip files are Yop2D projects: the engine downloads them from its "Examples" tab, or they can be opened with "Open a downloaded project".

## Ready-made objects (prefabs)

- Interface – animated health bar: Glossy health bar that drains smoothly: green, then orange, then flashing red when little life is left. Tap it to test (-10 each time); at zero it refills. The life is stored in the variable "vie" (0 to 100). Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – blue: Rectangular button (blue) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – discreet with glow: Plain, discreet button. On hover it lights up with a blue glow; on tap, a small bounce and ripples. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – spinning star: Golden button with a star that never stops spinning. On tap: sparks, a little bounce and a sound. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – yellow: Rectangular button (yellow) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – underlined text: Minimalist button: just text. On hover a line unfolds beneath it; on tap, a discreet ripple. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – pulsing neon: Dark button with a softly pulsing neon outline. On tap: light flash, sparks and a sound. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – ninja walking on it: Pixel-art button with a little ninja strolling along its top edge, overlapping the button. On tap: dust and a sound. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – pale pink: Rectangular button (pale pink) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – pale pink + animated text: Rectangular button (pale pink) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. The text tightens too. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – round play ▶: Round button with a ▶ and ripples that radiate continuously. On tap: bounce, confetti and a sound. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – pink: Rectangular button (pink) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – glass and shine: Glossy glass button. On hover a streak of light sweeps across it; on tap, sparks and a sound. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – green: Rectangular button (green) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Animated button – purple: Rectangular button (purple) with text. On hover it shrinks and sends out a shockwave. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Interface – pause window: A ⏸ button that pauses the game and opens a window with Resume, Restart and Quit over a dimmed background. The phone's back button opens it too. Texts and colours can be changed in the scene. Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Interface – ON/OFF switch: Slide switch: one tap flips it from OFF (grey) to ON (green) and back, with a small animation and a sound. It remembers its state in the variable "etat" (0 = off, 1 = on), perfect for "Sounds", "Music" or "Vibration". Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.
- Interface – popping score: Score counter with a star. Each time you score, the number swells for a moment and throws sparks with a sound. Tap it to test (+10); the score is stored in the variable "score". Open its scene to change the image, the text, the font or the nodes.

Prefabs are free (CC0) objects that already have their images, text and nodes. In the editor: Library, "Prefabs to download" tab (tick several, download, then "Add to the scene"). Own prefabs can be imported as a .zip (one scene) from the Resources panel. Step-by-step guide: https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/guides/en/prefabs.html

- [All nodes, English](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/en.html)
- [All nodes, Français](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/fr.html)

- [All nodes, Deutsch](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/de.html)
- [All nodes, Italiano](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/it.html)
- [All nodes, Português](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/pt.html)
- [All nodes, Русский](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/ru.html)
- [All nodes, 中文](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/zh.html)
- [All nodes, 日本語](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/ja.html)

Node categories and node names (as shown in the English editor):

- Events: On Start; Every frame; End of Click; On Object Click; Object Released; Object Held Down; Finger held down; Back button pressed; Drag Start; Drag End; Collision A/B; Exit Zone; On Hover; End of Hover; On Impact (Physics); When Variable Changes; Local Event; On Action Click (Adventure); If object touches Tag
- Scene & HUD: Go to scene; Go to scene (by name); Next scene; Previous scene; Restart the scene; Open a HUD; Close the HUD; Place a copy of a scene; Destroy the copies of a scene; Quit the game; Small message at the bottom of the screen; Write to the log (for debugging); Follow with camera; Camera limits; Camera smoothing; Screen flash; Screen tint; Vignette; Screen fade; Atmosphere (rain, snow, night…); Zoom the screen; Camera shake; Vibration; Save state; Restore state; Save variables to a file; Load variables from a file
- Time: Wait; Repeat; Countdown; Stop a timer; Game speed (slow motion); Pause the game; Resume the game; Hit stop
- Appearance & Objects: Move Object; Push object; Set a property; Rotation; Transparency; Visibility; Give a tag (object family); Bring to front / send back; Grow / shrink; Destroy Object; Destroy by Tag; Change Image; Modify Color; Generate clone (Spawner); Color Filter; Color blending (light effect); Mirror Effect / Invert; Lock / unlock the object; Background scrolling (depth); Link two objects; Glowing halo; Particle effect; Particles on / off; Particle burst; Change particle preset; Blink; Create a copy of the object; Shoot an object; Launch a guided missile (curve); Destroy the object after a delay (seconds); Set Progress; Screen wrap; Clamp to screen; Electrocution; Object trail; Create object; Fade
- Variables & Inventory: Modify Variable; Add to Variable; Keep a variable between two values; Random number; Add to inventory; Remove from inventory; If in inventory; Combine two objects
- Logic & Conditions: Condition; If joystick; If on ground; If moving; Call function; Call event; Sequence; Cooldown; If off-screen; If / Else; By value
- Texts & Dialogues: Modify Text; Show dialogue; Append to text
- Movements & AI: Play movement (steps); Stop the movement; Stop the object; Stop movements; Move forward continuously; Go to an object (path); Go to a point (path); Stop the path; Chase an object; Flee an object; Push at an angle; Impulse (jump); Change the behavior; Bounce around; Face towards; Glide to
- Grids and puzzles: Fill the grid; Play on the grid (match 3); Shuffle the grid; Shuffle places
- Transitions: Screen transition (circle, star…); Go to scene with a transition
- Animations: Play animation; Stop animation; Pause animation; Resume animation; Animation speed
- Audio: Play sound; Play music; Stop music
- Story and dialogues: Say a line; Ask a choice; Change the background; Pass through the scenery; Stop the passing images; Show / hide a character; Animate a character; Novel mode (full-screen text); SMS mode (phone conversation); Unlock an achievement; Replayable scene (gallery); End the story; Friendship (hearts); If the friendship…; Story title screen; Ask the player for a text (name…)
- Values (green wires): Random number; Object value; Variable value; Calculation; Distance between 2 objects
- Screen filters: Screen filter; Stop the filter

## Comparison with other engines

There are excellent game engines. Here is an honest comparison to help you choose, including what Yop2D does not do.

- Yop2D: Where you create: Android app (tablet, phone), works offline; How you program: Visual nodes, no code; 2D / 3D: 2D; Price: Free, no ads; sell your games freely; Your game runs on: Android (APK built on the device)
- GDevelop: Where you create: Computer, web browser, mobile app; How you program: Events, no code (JavaScript optional); 2D / 3D: 2D and 3D; Price: Free and open source; paid plans for more online services; Your game runs on: Android, iOS, web, computer (mobile builds made online)
- Construct 3: Where you create: Web browser (also on tablets); How you program: Event sheets, no code (JavaScript optional); 2D / 3D: Mainly 2D; Price: Paid subscription; limited free version; Your game runs on: Android, iOS, web, computer (mobile builds made online)
- Godot: Where you create: Computer, web browser, Android editor; How you program: Code (GDScript, C#); 2D / 3D: 2D and 3D; Price: Free and open source; Your game runs on: Android, iOS, web, computer
- Ren'Py: Where you create: Computer (Windows, macOS, Linux); How you program: Simple script (Ren'Py language, optional Python); 2D / 3D: 2D, specialised in visual novels; Price: Free and open source; Your game runs on: Computer, Android, iOS, web (mobile versions built on the computer)

Simplified summary as of October 2026. Engines change quickly: check each engine's website for details.

What Yop2D does not do (yet):

- Your games run on Android only: no iPhone, web or computer version.
- No AAB export yet, the format required to publish on Google Play. It is planned for a later version.
- 2D only.
- The community and the number of tutorials are still growing, and a few bugs are possible: fixes arrive fast, often within days.
- No scripting language for experienced programmers: everything is done with nodes.
- The engine is free, but its source code is not public.

When another engine is a better choice:

- You need iPhone, web or computer versions of your game: GDevelop, Construct or Godot.
- You want to learn real programming or make 3D games: Godot.
- You work on a computer and want a no-code engine with a large community: GDevelop or Construct.
- You are writing a long visual novel on a computer and want the reference tool, very complete, with a large community: Ren'Py.

## FAQ

### What is Yop2D?

Yop2D is a free, no-code 2D game engine for Android. It lets anyone create a complete video game on a tablet or phone with visual nodes, without programming knowledge, and export it as an APK directly on the device.

### Is Yop2D really free? Are there ads?

Yes, Yop2D is 100% free: no subscription, no in-app purchases, no hidden fees. There are no ads in Yop2D, and there never will be.

### Who owns the games I make? Can I sell them?

Your games belong to you. You can keep them, give them away, share them or sell them, without asking permission and without paying anything to Yop2D.

### Can I make a visual novel, like with Ren'Py?

Yes. Yop2D has nodes made for dialogue games: "Say a line" (character, emotion, text letter by letter), "Ask a choice" (one output per answer, timer, locked answers), "Change the background", "Ask the player for a text" (their name) and "Atmosphere" (rain, storm, snow, night…). Characters have a sheet with one picture per emotion; they blink and talk. Everything is done with your finger, no code, and the game can be in 9 languages. Open the "Choice story" template or the Firefly Night example to start. There is also a title screen with "Continue", autosave and 5 save slots, the ◀ Back button, endings to discover with a gallery, player settings, friendship hearts, read-aloud and a map of the whole story. The "My first story" guide shows how to start in 5 minutes. Characters can slide, grow, jump or shake ("Animate a character"), and there is a full-screen novel mode as well as a gallery of replayable scenes and music.

### Is there a Yop2D logo or watermark in my games?

No. The games you export contain no Yop2D logo, splash screen or watermark.

### Is Yop2D open source?

No. Yop2D is free to use, but its source code is not public. This changes nothing for your games: they are entirely yours.

### I don't know how to code. Is that a problem?

Not at all. Yop2D replaces code with visual nodes that you connect together. It is made for beginners and for creators who prefer to focus on their game. The beginner guides show you how, step by step.

### Which devices does Yop2D run on?

Android tablets and phones with Android 7.0 or newer. Tablets are the most comfortable; on phones, Yop2D works in landscape mode with a compact interface. There is no version for iPhone, iPad or computer.

### Do I need a computer or an internet connection?

No. Yop2D creates and exports your game as a standalone APK directly on your device, 100% offline. No cloud build, no account.

### Can I publish my game on Google Play?

Not directly yet. Yop2D exports APK files: you can install them, share them, or publish them on sites that accept APKs, such as itch.io. Google Play requires the AAB format signed with your own key: this export is planned for a later version.

### Can I play my Yop2D game on iPhone, on the web or on a computer?

No. Games made with Yop2D are Android apps. If you need other platforms, see the comparison for engines that support them.

### What kinds of games can I make?

2D games: platformers, top-down adventures, shooters, arcade and puzzle games, quizzes, interactive stories… The tile editor, physics, collisions, animations, dialogues, inventory and saving cover most needs. Yop2D does not make 3D games.

### Can I use my own images, sounds and music?

Yes. You import your own images, tilesets, animation frames, sound effects and music. Titles and text effects are created directly in the engine. The engine also includes a library of about 420 images (many animated), sound effects, music, fonts and ready-made titles, plus packs to download: no need to look elsewhere to get started.

### What languages is Yop2D available in?

The interface, the built-in help, the guides and the node reference are available in 9 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.

### How do I learn to use Yop2D?

Start with the "Your first game in 5 minutes" guide: it has you build a real little game step by step, showing you where to tap. Open the "Templates" tab: 50 small projects that each show a single thing, with an explanation on screen. Then play with the twenty-one example games and follow the beginner guides. The node reference explains all 166 nodes, and the YouTube channel, Discord and Telegram are there to help. In the engine, the "My animated hero" guide and its 4 step-by-step missions (☰ → Step-by-step missions) go even further, all the way to the game installed on your phone. The "Discover the editor" guide explains the interface: move, resize, rotate, lock, undo.

### What is a prefab in Yop2D?

A prefab is a ready-made object: it comes with its image, its text and its nodes already connected, for example an animated button. In the editor, open the Library, "⬇ Prefabs to download" tab, download one or several, then tap "＋ Add to the scene". Prefabs are free and CC0. You can edit them as you like and import your own from a .zip file. Not to be confused with "Scenes as objects", which lets you reuse one of your own scenes. A step-by-step guide exists: "How to add a ready-made object?". Each prefab you add becomes its own scene: touch it in the Scenes list (shown under the scene that uses it) to change the image, the colour, the text or the nodes, and every copy follows. Interface pieces are offered too: ON/OFF switch, animated health bar, popping score and pause window.

### How do I resume a mission halfway through?

Open your project, tap ☰ then "Step-by-step missions" and choose the mission. The bubble starts again from the first step: tap "Skip" to jump over the steps you've already done, or "◀" to go back to a previous step. A finished mission shows a ✓ and can be done again.

### Why does Android show a warning when I install the APK?

Because the APK is downloaded outside the Play Store. Tap More details, then Install anyway. You can also join the closed test on Google Play: how to become a tester.

### Does Yop2D collect data?

Yop2D sends anonymous usage statistics: when it is opened and closed, how long it was used, and crash reports (type of error only), with the app version, Android version and device language. The country is estimated from the connection, without storing the IP address. No personal data and nothing from your projects. You can turn it off on the home screen, and the games you export send nothing. Details: privacy policy.

### Is Yop2D finished?

Yop2D is in active development and in closed testing on Google Play. It is already usable to make complete games, but bugs are possible: export your projects regularly as a backup, and report problems on Discord or Telegram.

### Who makes Yop2D?

Yop2D is made by an independent developer, with the feedback of its community of testers.

### How is Yop2D different from GDevelop, Construct or Godot?

Yop2D is designed to work entirely on an Android tablet or phone, without code, without internet and without a computer, and it stays free with no ads. In return, it only makes 2D games for Android. See the detailed comparison.

### Can Yop2D be used in class?

Yes. Yop2D is free, with no ads, no account and no personal data, and it works offline on ordinary Android tablets. School mode (the 🎓 button on the start screen) simplifies the interface, hides violent content and external links, and is protected by a teacher code. Teachers can write to us to adapt Yop2D to their class.

### Is Yop2D suitable for children?

Yes, from about 8 years old with an adult (parent or teacher), and on their own from 11-12. The built-in guides show where to tap, the templates explain one thing at a time and the settings are written in plain words. School mode makes the interface even simpler and gentler.

### How do I change my game's icon?

Open ☰ → Game settings → Game icon, pick an image, adjust the zoom and position, then save. The icon is applied when you build the APK; without a chosen icon, the Yop2D logo is kept.

### How do I create my own music?

In the Assets window, touch the "Music" button (Android 10 or newer). Place ready-made blocks on the 4 tracks (melody, chords, bass, drums), or build your own in the note editor, listen on a loop, then touch "Create the sound (.ogg)": the file is saved in the Sounds folder of your choice and plays with the "Jouer la musique" node. The instruments are free to use (CC0). A step-by-step guide exists: "How to create your own music?".

### What can Yop2D do today?

In the editor: undo and redo (in the scene and in the Blueprint), automatic saving, copy-paste, folders to organise objects and files, grid snapping, several scenes, instant test with the ▶ button and a "Check my game" button that spots what you forgot. To create: 166 nodes, tile editor, animation editor, music maker, dialogue games with save slots, screen filters, particles, pathfinding, 50 templates and step-by-step guides. To share: APK export on the device with your own icon, version number and launch image. Current limits: Android and 2D only, and an independent developer who updates the engine very often.
